status: Written before any scoring with these templates or facts. novel_author and invention_inventor are identical to v1, company_founder identical to v2, validity_rules identical to v1/v2. Four relations are new.
design_rules: No edit prompt begins with the subject (lesson of study 3462 / hypothesis H-pos0, confirmed by 3467 for all three methods).
Within a relation every object appears in at most one fact, so the fact whose old object is a given new object is unique.
A fact is excluded at construction if its old object's name occurs in its subject (e.g. 'Honda NSX' -> 'Honda'): the forward read would test string copying, not the fact.

CounterFact lists several subjects for some capitals (e.g. Berlin: Nazi Germany, Weimar Republic, Germany, ...). All are kept as candidates with dup_group = the old object, and screening keeps at most one INCLUDED fact per dup_group: the one whose best valid reverse_old route gives the subject the highest full-answer log-probability on the unedited model (ties: lowest CounterFact case_id). This uses pre-edit reads only.

validity_rules.include_fact_if: edit prompt valid AND >=2 of the other 3 forward routes valid AND >=1 valid reverse_old AND >=1 valid reverse_new AND >=1 valid control

consistency_contract.edit_semantics: Every edit replaces the tuple (s, r, o) by (s, r, o*). It is an UPDATE, not an INSERT: after it, (s, r, o) is no longer true.
consistency_contract.forward: Every valid forward path must return o* at rank 1 (Q1). o at rank 1 on a forward path is a stale read (Q2).
consistency_contract.reverse_old: A reverse path naming o asks for the subjects of o. After the update s is not one of them, so s at rank 1 is a stale read (Q2) for every relation, whatever its cardinality. Another subject of o at rank 1 is legitimate.
consistency_contract.reverse_new_if_inverse_functional: If each object has exactly one subject (1:1), the reverse path naming o* must return s at rank 1 after the update; anything else is a violation. The update also conflicts with o*'s own fact (o* now has two subjects): this is an integrity-constraint violation of the edit request itself and is reported as such.
consistency_contract.reverse_new_if_inverse_non_functional: If an object can have many subjects, s need not reach rank 1 on the reverse path naming o* (o*'s best-known subject may stay first). s must become more likely (log-probability rises); a fall is a violation.
consistency_contract.controls: The correct answer of a neighbouring fact (same relation) and of o*'s own fact must stay at rank 1 (except o*'s own fact under an inverse-functional relation, see above). The rise of o* on these reads is reported as drift, not as a violation.
